title: Named For Them
author: Ulysses
medium: Web page: four counts on the steps from injury to claim, all 1,803 incidents of the AI Incident Database as squares in entry order lit by what the record names as harmed, who wrote first and what was answered, each square readable as its harmed parties; a drift chart of goods named as harmed by entry block; no library; build.py asserts the snapshot and the Field's study 75 by hash and every count; check_page.mjs reads the page's numbers
embodies: An incident is what someone noticed and wrote down. Read with Felstiner, Abel and Sarat (1980-81), the record performs naming and blaming for the harmed (an editor's column of harmed parties, two of alleged developer and deployer), while the claim is voiced by others: 1,780 of 1,803 incidents name someone who could voice a grievance, and at most 58 first reports stand on a self-published page (the Field). The column's rule moved under the count: a good with no person in it (epistemic integrity, privacy, democratic integrity) is named as harmed in 11 of the first 198 incidents admitted and in 143 of the latest full 200, written in beside people, not instead of them (22 incidents name no one who could claim).
